pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are 0 and that the CHECK constraint rejects 2. migrations/0002_add_done.sql is correct.
'AC-2' test covers / and ?view=open, filtered and in id order.
'AC-3' test covers done-only, ✓ prefix, id order (marked 3 then 1).
'AC-4' test covers all items in order with ✓ only on done ones.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav markup for each view and the default.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values. Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.

The behaviour is implemented, and an untitled test does exercise it. But the final commit 88e7bc8 removed 'AC-7' from that test's title. It also rewrote the acceptance item to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. No test names AC-7, and the review mark demonstrates nothing, so the item is unmet. The commit edits the acceptance item after the go, and the spec records no decision for it.
traffic/routes.json lists both views. The 'AC-8' test asserts they are in the file.

findings.what: Commit 88e7bc8 ('Follow-up edits') changed the AC-7 acceptance item after the go. It appended 'verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence, with no owner decision or date in the spec. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable step. The edit also made the item's sentence read oddly.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit to the owner-approved wording. Keep AC-7 as a test-proven item, and record any real change as a dated owner decision.

findings.what: The same commit renamed the test from 'AC-7: ...' to 'an empty table says so...', so no test names AC-7. The test would still catch broken behaviour, but the rename removed the link between AC-7 and its test.
The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'. This is false: a later commit edited an acceptance item and renamed its test.
findings.fix: Revert the edits, or disclose them and the owner's decision in the PR.

lenses.note: The spec exists and has the owner's go. The behaviour matches the decisions: open is the default view and the view is a query parameter. Nothing beyond the ask, apart from the traffic-check regex relaxation that routes with a query need.
AC-7 was edited after the go with no recorded decision. All six state-table rows have tests.
Tests assert behaviour. AC-7's test lost its name in the last commit. I did not run the suite. No .github/workflows were checked, and the tests need the Workers runtime.
README describes the views and the default of open. The 400 for other view values is not mentioned there, which is minor.
The implementation is sound: Object.hasOwn guards the lookup, the SQL is built from fixed strings, and the empty-table fallback works. The traffic check relaxation still rejects spaces and #.
The view value is allow-listed and never reaches SQL. Titles are HTML-escaped. No planted instructions found.
The page is a bare server-rendered list; no CSS or UI component files are in the diff.
No browser flow or UI component files in the diff.
The claims 'Changed after the go: nothing' and 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' are false because of the last commit.
